assumptions: The zero-cost trade guard is the check whose triggering is governed by the intent.
A legitimate trade is one in which no side receives tokens without sending any.

unresolved.description: The report does not quote the exact zero-cost check expression or its operands, so the guard's internal condition cannot be bound beyond the stated intent that it should trigger only when one side receives tokens without sending any.

The report does not specify whether matched base and quote amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state, so the disjoint-bits precondition is encoded as the stated observable condition.

limitations: The intent's 'only when' is encoded as the guard triggering under the one-side-receives-without-sending condition; the converse prohibition (guard must not trigger otherwise) is captured only through the separate impact witness.
The disjoint-bits precondition is represented as a single grounded Boolean because the report states the condition qualitatively with illustrative examples rather than a single numeric predicate.
